equation_summary: Two coupled additive accumulators sharing one slot-decay. When g is not supplied it is derived from the slot logits: z=logcumsumexp(s), g_t=z_{t-1}-z_t (per-slot, so exp(g_t)=Z_{t-1}/Z_t) and s_t:=exp(s_t-z_t)=softmax(s)_t (cumulative-softmax normalized slot gates). Stage 1: hk_t = hk_{t-1}*exp(g_t)[None,:] + k_t ⊗ s_t; ok_t = (scale*q_t)ᵀ hk_t (a [M] slot vector); interstage qv_t = softmax(ok_t) over slots (external). Stage 2: hv_t = hv_{t-1}*exp(g_t)[:,None] + s_t ⊗ v_t; o_t = qv_tᵀ hv_t. Both are additive (c=0) channel/slot-decayed accumulations with after-update read; neither uses the delta correction (v - kᵀM k), so each is U2.A-with-channel-decay in transition, not the canonical delta law.
state_shape: two matrices: hk [K,M] (key x slot) and hv [M,V] (slot x value), per head
gate_scope: channel (per-slot) data-dependent decay exp(g_t) identical in both stages; gate derived from cumulative-softmax of slot logits when not passed explicitly
normalization: external interstage softmax over slot scores ok; stage-1 write weights s are cumulative-softmax normalized; no denominator state
ledger_verdicts: CONFIRM two-stage structure: B[K2 stage-1 slot summary hk] ; E[slot softmax qv=softmax(ok)] ; B[K2 stage-2 value summary hv] matches naive_recurrent_abc (naive.py:47-67).

CONFIRM coupling: the SAME per-slot decay g enters stage 1 as g_i[..., None, :] (slot axis on columns) and stage 2 as g_i[..., :, None] (slot axis on rows), and stage-2's keys are the stage-1 write gates s — the coupling is a typed tensor edge plus shared gate operand, not a shared transition algebra.

CONFIRM ledger blocker 'two calls cannot be replaced by one generic K2 by name': states hk[K,M] and hv[M,V] have different shapes/axes and the interstage softmax is data-dependent on hk, so no single canonical K2 call covers both.

CORRECT (refinement): both stages are ADDITIVE (v=s or v=v written directly, no kᵀM retrieval correction), so each stage is U2.A (additive, channel-decayed) rather than U2.D; the ledger's 'B[K2 ...]' is fine but any descriptor must record c=0 plus the cumulative-softmax-derived gate (logcumsumexp), which is a data-dependent gate provenance the canonical K2 gate field must accept.
direction_justification: ABC is exactly two U2.A-family calls joined by a family-generic typed structure: an interstage softmax on the first call's output feeding the second call's queries, with a shared slot-decay operand — a cross-call composition (cf. ledger's own reuse matrix row 'Cross-call output combination 048/049'), not a new core mixer.
open_questions: Is the cumulative-softmax-derived gate (g from logcumsumexp(s)) expressible as a closed K2 gate-provenance descriptor, or must gates be passed as precomputed external operands (the layer always passes s only; chunk.py derives g internally)?
Chunked kernels (chunk.py) need verification that they reproduce the naive two-pass coupling exactly, including initial_state handling for both hk and hv.
